text:
William Stromgren got his first NHL goal on Monday, and it helped decide a game his team spent most of the night chasing. The Calgary winger, drafted 45th overall by the Flames in 2021, tipped one in with a bat at 9:14 of the third period for a 2-0 lead, and CGY held on to beat San Jose 2-1. The first goal belonged to Adam Klapka, who was never drafted and made the NHL as a free agent. His first-period wrist shot carried only a 5 percent chance of going in.

Calgary won despite being outplayed. San Jose attempted 71 shots to CGY's 41, and our model, which replays every shot to see how often a team would win, gave the Sharks a 66 percent chance of deserving the result. Expected goals, a measure of the quality of chances, favored SJS 2.88 to 2.23, and the Sharks controlled the third period 1.16 to 0.62. Dustin Wolf is why it didn't matter. He stopped 26 of 27 shots, and by our count that saved about 1.9 more goals than the chances against him should have allowed, which earned him first star. Yaroslav Askarov was fine at the other end, stopping 20 of 22 shots. Will Smith had a 25 percent look in the third that missed the net.

Sam Dickinson cut it to 2-1 at 11:57 of the third, set up by Jacob Trouba and Kiefer Sherwood, but San Jose never found the equalizer. Neither power play scored, with each team going 0 for 3. Calgary leaves with a win it did not entirely earn on the chance count. San Jose leaves with the better underlying game and nothing to show for it.
